acceptance_criteria.description: Generated manifest schema includes a strict official Windows mGBA 0.10.5 emulator contract with the pinned archive and executable digests; generator and launcher deny unknown, malformed, wrong-version, wrong-platform, and wrong-digest values.

The launcher hashes the guarded executable before either probe or gameplay execution and refuses a mismatch without creating an mGBA process; an executable replacement or identity drift between validation and launch is detected before gameplay code runs.

On Windows, both probe and gameplay mGBA are created inside a kill-on-close Job at CreateProcess time via windows-spawn =0.1.0; cancellation, parent/control loss, startup failure, timeout, normal root exit with surviving descendants, and forced stop terminate and reap the complete process tree under bounded deadlines.

The containment abstraction integrates with existing SupervisedChildren event/stop APIs without changing mGBA argv, sidecar behavior, lease/recovery ordering, or non-Windows deterministic test behavior.

Windows tests use a helper root plus delayed-marker or retained-handle descendant to prove no descendant escapes on probe timeout, cancellation, drop, startup failure, or forced stop, while exact argv/environment and bounded output behavior remain covered.
Generator tests, launcher tests, formatting, launcher clippy with warnings denied, locked metadata, and diff checks pass with changes confined to owned_files.

closed_decisions: The only accepted stock runtime for this slice is the official mGBA 0.10.5 Windows x64 Qt executable. Pin executable SHA-256 5a3c98c2984dd04bd0d7c9378cdfae937ae0d73a196c880bb2eecf3b254af247 and archive provenance SHA-256 b497a57c7d9093834dadc64f33a90f7c411439c21fdb8a0143255a45ea37563a in the generated deny-unknown-fields compatibility manifest. Reject an executable digest mismatch before executing --version or gameplay.
Bump the generated bridge manifest schema when adding the bounded emulator contract. Keep ROM game build, regional identity registry, save schema, bridge ABI, and game protocol values unchanged.

Pin windows-spawn exactly at =0.1.0 as a Windows-only workspace dependency. Use its safe public API and creation-time PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST Job attachment; do not use post-spawn AssignProcessToJobObject, process-wrap, taskkill as the containment proof, or repository-owned unsafe Rust.

Use one dedicated in-process blocking supervisor per mGBA process to own windows-spawn Child/Job state and expose a small bounded async command/event boundary to Tokio. Parent cancellation, channel closure, supervisor drop, startup failure, timeout, and forced stop must terminate and reap the entire Job tree. Never detach a supervisor thread.

Apply the same contained boundary to the --version probe and the long-lived gameplay process. Preserve exact shell-free argv, PATH-only inherited environment, null/piped stdio bounds, stock mGBA 0.10.5 version validation, and the existing public launcher behavior on non-Windows test targets.

Close the executable path substitution interval: hash a bounded regular executable while holding the existing deny-write/delete Windows executable guard, keep that guard through each contained spawn, and revalidate the pinned digest immediately before gameplay launch. A changed or unbound identity fails before mGBA code executes.
This unit provides force-stop/job containment only. Do not invent authenticated graceful shutdown semantics or edit sidecar/session control behavior; that is a dependent unit.

Do not claim that Job containment solves the separately tracked handle-relative staged-save deletion/ACL blocker. It may fix the proven empty coop-rom-* directory ownership leak if it can do so within existing owned process code and tests without weakening recovery retention.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit sidecar, session lifecycle, main CLI, cloud/server/protocol/save, bridge/Lua, ROM, regional identity data, documentation, or orchestration state outside owned_files.

Do not accept another mGBA binary/version/platform digest, permit a hash override, execute an unverified binary, fall back to direct std/tokio mGBA spawn on Windows, or use PID-only taskkill as successful descendant cleanup evidence.

Do not add unsafe Rust, allow attributes, a shell, command strings, secrets in argv/environment/protocol output, unbounded channels/reads/writes/threads/retries, or a supervisor that can outlive launcher ownership.
Do not alter checkpoint/control semantics, release ordering, ROM args, save formats, region-qualified identities, or manifest values unrelated to the emulator contract.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact Git remotes, create/remove worktrees, or revert edits made by another worker.
objective: Pin the supported official mGBA 0.10.5 Windows executable identity and ensure both version probing and gameplay launch occur inside a kill-on-close Windows Job from the emulator's first instruction, with bounded async supervision and descendant-reap evidence.

return_when: Every acceptance criterion is resolved and every required verification command has a recorded outcome.
windows-spawn or the existing launcher API cannot meet creation-time containment without a change outside owned_files.
A concrete Windows process, dependency, or executable-identity blocker prevents safe progress within the execution budget.
